title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier-Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared-Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study-cnd-2026-001) to test whether a verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves oracle pass rates for LLM-produced network configurations on vendor-diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. Key frozen design choices included: paired design with Npairs=200, generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair consumed by both conditions), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic emulator validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, repair budget ≤1 call/task, and primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Execution completed as preregistered (planned_episode_count=400; completed_episode_count=400; model_calls_used=200; failed_episode_count=0). Both baseline and guarded conditions produced oracle-passing configurations for all 200 pairs (baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200), giving an absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.00). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics caused the same generated candidate to be used by both conditions and every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and hashes) and interpret the null confirmatory result as a design-bound outcome that highlights the critical role of independent-generation semantics, task difficulty, oracle coverage, and repair budget in revealing measurable pipeline benefits. We conclude with reproducibility-focused recommendations for future guarded-pipeline evaluations.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate natural-language intent into device configurations to simplify NetOps, but documented failure modes (hallucination, unsafe ordering, vendor-idiom errors) motivate verifier-anchored architectures (generate→validate→repair). We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to test whether a verifier-assisted pipeline increases oracle pass rates relative to unconstrained generation. The research question (preregistered) is: under the frozen experimental plan, does the verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase the oracle pass rate (primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and deterministic, artifact-backed execution manifest; (2) archival release of all model calls, validator traces, and analysis artifacts; (3) an artifact-grounded report showing a null confirmatory outcome under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and a diagnostic discussion of why the guarded pipeline was not exercised.
sections.related_work: Prior work explores LLM-based intent→configuration translation, verifier-augmented generation, and repair loops. Representative systems and findings include NetConfEval and intent-translators that test translation quality [Chang et al.; Wang et al.], constraint-based adaptation improving reliability (MeshAgent) [Zhou et al.], and verifier-grounded repair workflows that improve semantic correctness in other domains (StruSpec) [Ding]. These works motivate verifier-assisted pipelines; our study differs by preregistering a deterministic paired protocol, freezing generation semantics, and publishing a fully auditable artifact set so that observed null effects can be traced to explicit design choices.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: preregistration id study-cnd-2026-001 (sha256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). Confirmatory design: paired binary comparison (baseline vs guarded) with Npairs=200, protocol buckets BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN balanced, vendor stratification (Cisco/Juniper/Arista), and complexity stratification (simple/complex) as described in the preregistration. Crucial frozen semantics: generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate: a single candidate was generated per pair during a shared stage and consumed by both conditions. Model/adapter/validator: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider openai_responses; configuration archived at execution/model_configuration.json, sha256 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulation-based oracle). Repair policy: at most one repair call per task (preregistered). Execution logging and artifacts: every model call, provider trace, raw response, and validator trace recorded; execution manifest archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; full hash manifest included). Analysis plan: primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed via paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact two-sided McNemar test; primary-missingness policy = complete-pair analysis (pairs with provider/infrastructure failures would be excluded and logged).
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count=400; completed_episode_count=400; failed_episode_count=0; model_calls_used=200 (shared-initial generation produced one generation per pair); execution manifest verifies these counts (see execution/execution_manifest.json and its hashes). Confirmatory analysis (artifact-backed): complete_pairs=200; baseline_successes=200/200 (baseline_success_rate=1.0); guarded_successes=200/200 (guarded_success_rate=1.0); absolute paired difference = 0.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Deterministic reconciliation confirms marginal and pair accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha256 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174). Repair-stage activity: repair calls invoked = 0; repair_applied_count = 0; the guarded repair stage was never exercised because the shared initial candidate passed the deterministic oracle in every pair. Representative artifacts: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b) and paired shared candidate execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256 f8de4d6e1a625e42ba4907440b4377c78949ed56446e5c73030bc267e56abfaf) illustrate the canonical, fully passing shared candidate.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preregistered null confirmatory result is definitive for the exact frozen design: because generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate and every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the guarded repair path could not provide additional benefit in this run. This is a design-bound null result—it does not imply verifier-assisted architectures are ineffective generally. The study highlights three design axes that control observable improvement: (1) generation independence (shared vs independent generation); (2) task difficulty and oracle coverage (the synthetic task bank here was solvable by the shared generator and oracle); and (3) repair budget and iteration policy (we limited repairs to ≤1 call/task). Methodological lessons. (i) When evaluating guarded pipelines, preregister and report generation semantics explicitly; shared-generation semantics can conceal pipeline effect. (ii) Pre-evaluate oracle coverage and task difficulty to avoid ceiling effects; our artifacts include oracle-coverage diagnostics. (iii) When the primary estimand becomes uninformative because of ceiling (baseline = 100%), report the exact counts, stop inference for the preregistered contrast, and present the result as a design-bound outcome. Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial semantics intentionally removes independent generation variance and therefore hides repair demand; this choice was preregistered and is recorded in the manifest. Construct validity: the deterministic emulator oracle enforces explicit syntactic and semantic predicates but may not expose all production failure modes. External validity: single-model scope (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic emulation limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: with complete_pairs=200 and unanimous passes, inferential statistics correctly show no paired difference under the frozen design.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered and artifact-backed frozen design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task bank Npairs=200), both baseline and guarded conditions passed the oracle on every paired task; the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), so no measurable benefit could be observed. We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, model-call traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per-file hashes) so others can reproduce, rerun with independent-generation semantics, increase repair budgets, or select higher-difficulty tasks. Our primary methodological recommendation: explicitly preregister generation semantics (shared vs independent) because that choice materially affects the observable efficacy of verifier-assisted repair pipelines and, when shared-generation is used, can produce ceiling effects that preclude detecting repair benefits.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact-backed):

This master prompt launched the autonomous post-lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the master prompt before the autonomy lock; all other substantive research steps described in this paper were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock.
- Preregistration: study-cnd-2026-001 preregistration (sha256: a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) describing frozen hypotheses, analysis plan, sampling, stopping, generation semantics, and repair budget.
- Models and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) used via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). The run recorded provider-call traces for every model invocation (execution/provider_calls/*) and raw responses (execution/responses/*) with per-file SHA-256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest.
- Generation semantics and important frozen choice: generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (preregistered). Under this semantics one generated candidate was produced per pair and consumed by both baseline and guarded conditions; this choice is central to the observed outcome. The execution manifest records that model_calls_used = 200 (one shared-generation per 200 pairs) and planned_episode_count = 400 (two episodes per pair), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0 (see execution/execution_manifest.json and its hash in the artifact bundle).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulator-based oracle) was used to score candidates; all validator traces and scoring artifacts are archived under execution/scoring/ (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b).
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. In this run repair calls invoked = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 because every shared initial candidate passed the oracle; these counts are recorded in the execution and scoring artifacts.
- Preregistered analysis executor and settings: paired_binary_analysis_v1 with paired bootstrap (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; bootstrap_seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two-sided test. Confirmatory artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Execution and reproducibility procedures: all prompts, model outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring files, manifests, and analysis artifacts were immutably recorded and their SHA-256 hashes are listed in the execution manifest. Deterministic reconciliation confirms accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha256 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174).
- Human involvement: the Research Director selected topic family and pre-locked the master prompt and rehearsed infrastructure prior to autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock, all literature review, question selection, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed autonomously. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Any pre-lock development artifacts were not used as final-study evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post-lock workflow.
- Deviations and failures: none relevant to the primary confirmatory analysis; no provider/model-identifier drift occurred; no pairs were excluded; repair stage was not triggered (repair calls invoked = 0). All deviations (none) and the full manifest are available in the artifact bundle.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic task bank of 200); results do not generalize beyond these frozen choices.

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics eliminated independent sampling variance between baseline and guarded conditions and therefore prevented the guarded pipeline from exercising repairs in this run; this design choice was preregistered and materially caused the observed null effect.
Synthetic emulated tasks and a deterministic emulator-based oracle do not fully represent production heterogeneity (real devices, vendor-image idiosyncrasies, transient runtime faults).
Single-model experiment limits generality across LLM families, instruction-tuning, and deployment-specific behaviors.
Repair budget was restricted to one repair call per preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (coverage gaps) remain possible; oracle-coverage diagnostics are included in the artifact bundle and flagged where applicable.
